terms.gloss: a vine leaf; the leaves of a vine
evidence: Hor. C. 4.8.33: ōrnātus viridī tempora pampinō
terms.comment: Lewis & Short gives the word two senses: first a young shoot of a vine (see vine shoot), then a vine leaf, the foliage of a vine. Used of foliage it is often plural or collective; a single leaf can be pampinī folium, as in Plautus. Also feminine.

phrases.latin: Involvolum, quae in pampinī foliō intorta implicat sē.
phrases.english: The leaf-roller, which wraps itself up, rolled in a vine leaf.

phrases.latin: heu, male tum mītīs dēfendet pampinus ūvās
phrases.english: alas, the vine leaves will then be poor protection for the ripening grapes
Liber, his temples decked with green vine leaves
